Internal: jload()'s note on variables of numbers made text by a few cells

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_marker_note.Rd

Ruling R31, question 5 (Session 380): the values that are not numbers, each quoted with its count, then the jload() call as typed with na = naming them, which reads them as missing and the variables as numbers. It replaces the load scan's block for these variables, whose declaration left the variable text.

Usage

.jst_marker_note(marks, vars, line, obj_name = NULL, labels = NULL)

Arguments

marks

From .jst_csv_type_columns() or .jst_marker_columns().

vars

The data frame's variable names, as loaded.

line

The jload() line with na =, indented.

obj_name

The data frame's name, for the base R lines.

labels

The variables' labels, parallel to marks, NA where there is none; NULL for none.

Value

Character(1).

Details

Since Session 381 (Fix Slate 24, the (S380) item): a sheet's variable that also holds a number stored as text (stored above zero, from .jst_marker_columns()) stays text after a reload with na =, so its lines are base R's instead (.jst_numeric_lines()): its cells made missing, then as.numeric(), then its label put back if jload() gave it one. Beside a variable the reload does serve, the reload comes first – its na = names every value in the note, so the stored variable's cells are already missing – and the stored variable gets only the as.numeric() line.
